title: Euclid's division lemma
competency: Write any division as a = (b × q) + r with 0 ≤ r < b and use it to solve problems.

keywords.def: For a ≥ 0 and b > 0 there are unique q and r with a = b × q + r, 0 ≤ r < b. Also called Euclid's division lemma.
The number being divided: a in a = b × q + r.
The number you divide by: b in a = b × q + r.
How many whole times the divisor fits: q in a = b × q + r.
What is left over after dividing: r in a = b × q + r, with 0 ≤ r < b.
a is divisible by b when the remainder is 0.

en.text: To divide a by b, see how many whole groups of b fit in a. That number is the quotient q. What is left over is the remainder r. So a = (b × q) + r. The remainder is always smaller than b. When the remainder is 0, a is divisible by b.

screens.title: Sharing books
screens.text: A bookshop shares 115 books equally among 8 students.
screens.ask: How many books are left over? Take a guess.
screens.after:
Count in 8s: 8 × 14 = 112.
8 × 15 = 120 is more than 115, so 14 is the most each gets.
115 − 112 = 3 books are left.
The 3 left is less than 8, so no one can get another book.

screens.title: Guess the remainder first
screens.text: You will divide 128 by 6. Before you divide, think about what can be left.
screens.ask: Remainders when dividing by 6: which remainders are possible?
screens.why:
The remainder is what is left after making full groups of 6.
If 6 or more were left, you could make one more group.
So the remainder can only be 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5.
Example: 128 = 6 × 21 + 2, remainder 2.
("0 to 6" is wrong: a remainder of 6 makes one more group.)
screens.clue: If 6 were left, could you make one more group of 6?

screens.title: Theorem 1.1
paras: Take a non-negative integer a and a positive integer b.
Then there are unique non-negative integers q and r.
They satisfy a = (b × q) + r, with 0 ≤ r < b.
This is Euclid's division lemma. It is also called the division algorithm.

screens.title: Try the division algorithm
screens.ask: Move the sliders. Watch q and r. Can you ever make r reach b?
screens.note: r is always less than b. The check always gives back a.

screens.title: Name the parts
defs: a = (b × q) + r with 0 ≤ r < b. Also called Euclid's division lemma.
b, the number you divide by.
q, how many whole times b fits in a.
r, what is left over. Always 0 ≤ r < b.

screens.title: Find the remainder
screens.text: Parts of a division: in 47 = 6 × 7 + 5, which number is the remainder?
screens.why:
Match the form a = (b × q) + r.
a = 47 is the dividend. b = 6 is the divisor.
q = 7 is the quotient: 7 full groups of 6.
r = 5 is the remainder. Check: 5 < 6.
So the remainder is 5.
screens.clue: It is the number added at the end, and it is less than the divisor.

screens.text: Write each division in the form a = (b × q) + r.
steps: The quotient is 0 and the remainder is 5.

screens.title: Divisible
paras: a is divisible by b when the remainder is 0.
In Example 1(c), 12 = 3 × 4 + 0. So 12 is divisible by 3.

screens.title: Why not 6?
screens.text: The remainder rule: why can the remainder never be 6 when you divide by 6?
opts: Because 6 more makes another full group
screens.ans: Because 6 more makes another full group
screens.why:
Picture 6 objects left over.
They make one more full group of 6.
Then the quotient goes up by 1 and the remainder goes down to 0.
So the remainder is always less than the divisor: r < 6.
screens.clue: Picture 6 leftover objects. What could you do with them?

screens.title: Fill the remainder
screens.why:
Step 1: 7 × 14 = 98.
Step 2: 100 − 98 = 2.
Check: 2 < 7, so it is a true remainder.
So 100 = 7 × 14 + 2.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: Division form: 17 = 5 × 2 + 7 is the division of 17 by 5.
screens.why:
The sum is right: 5 × 2 + 7 = 17.
But the remainder must be less than the divisor: 0 ≤ r < 5.
7 is not less than 5, so one more 5 fits.
The right form is 17 = 5 × 3 + 2.
So the statement is false.
screens.worked: 7 is not less than 5, so one more 5 fits. 17 = 5 × 3 + 2.

screens.title: Buying bread
screens.text: Hana has 50 birr. One bread costs 6 birr. She buys as many as she can.
screens.ask: Find the remainder in birr: Hana has ___ birr left.
screens.why:
Step 1: find the biggest multiple of 6 not above 50.
6 × 8 = 48. 6 × 9 = 54 is too much.
Step 2: 50 − 48 = 2.
So 50 = 6 × 8 + 2. She buys 8 breads and has 2 birr left.
screens.clue: Find the biggest multiple of 6 that is not more than 50.

items.text: A bookshop shares 115 books equally among 8 students.
items.ask: Find the quotient: each student gets ___ books.
items.why:
Divide 115 by 8.
8 × 14 = 112 and 8 × 15 = 120 (too much).
115 − 112 = 3 left over.
So 115 = 8 × 14 + 3. Each student gets 14 books.

Take away the remainder first: 128 − 2 = 126.
Divide: 126 ÷ 6 = 21.
Check: 6 × 21 + 2 = 126 + 2 = 128.
So the quotient is 21.

items.text: a = 14, b = 3. Find q with 14 = (3 × q) + r and 0 ≤ r < 3.
items.why:
Count the 3s in 14: 3 × 4 = 12, and 3 × 5 = 15 is too much.
14 − 12 = 2, and 2 < 3.
So 14 = 3 × 4 + 2. The quotient is 4.

items.text: a = 116, b = 7. Find q and r with 0 ≤ r < 7.
items.why:
Step 1: 7 × 16 = 112.
Step 2: 116 − 112 = 4.
Check: 4 < 7.
So 116 = 7 × 16 + 4. The remainder is 4.

items.text: Division algorithm with a < b: for a = 25 and b = 36, which is the division in the right form?
items.why:
25 is less than 36, so 36 fits 0 times.
q = 0 and r = 25. Check: 0 ≤ 25 < 36.
So 25 = 36 × 0 + 25.
(25 = 36 × 1 − 11 subtracts, but the form needs + r with r ≥ 0.)

items.text: a = 987, b = 16. Find q and r with 0 ≤ r < 16.
Remainder 3: which positive integers leave remainder 3 when divided by 4?
items.why:
The numbers have the form 4q + 3.
q = 0 gives 3, q = 1 gives 7, q = 2 gives 11, and so on.
3 is included: 3 = 4 × 0 + 3, and 3 < 4.
So the list is 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, …
(Starting at 7 forgets q = 0.)
items.clue: Write each number as 4 × q + 3. Can q be 0?

items.text: A man has 68 Birr. Each item costs 7 Birr. He wants 5 Birr left in his pocket.
items.ask: Word problem with the division algorithm: the largest number of items he can buy is ___.
items.why:
He keeps 5 Birr, so he can spend 68 − 5 = 63 Birr.
Divide by the price: 63 = 7 × 9 + 0.
So he can buy 9 items.
Check: 9 × 7 = 63, and 63 + 5 = 68 Birr.
items.clue: First take away the 5 Birr he keeps.
items.worked: 68 − 5 = 63 Birr to spend. 63 ÷ 7 = 9 with remainder 0. So 9 items.

test.text: Division algorithm: in a = (b × q) + r, which must be true?
test.why:
The remainder is what is left after full groups of b.
It cannot be negative, so r ≥ 0.
If r were b or more, one more group would fit, so r < b.
So 0 ≤ r < b.

test.ask: Find the remainder: when 59 is divided by 8, the remainder is ___.
test.why:
8 × 7 = 56 and 8 × 8 = 64 (too much).
59 − 56 = 3.
So 59 = 8 × 7 + 3. The remainder is 3.
